questions.question: Explain the ways through which media management ensures efficient resource allocation in a
questions.solution_html:
• media organisation.
  • Media management ensures efficient resource allocation by engaging in strategic planning to
  • align financial, technological, and human resources with the organization's high-priority goals and
  • audience needs. It uses continuous monitoring and data analytics to evaluate resource utilization,
  • identify bottlenecks, and make necessary adjustments to budgets and personnel assignments,
  • minimizing waste and maximizing return on investment.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Define the role of a news editor in a media organization.
questions.solution_html:
• The News Editor plays a critical managerial and content-gatekeeping role within a media
  • organization, overseeing the daily production and quality of news content across various platforms
  • (print, broadcast, or digital).
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What do you mean by chain ownership in media? Give one Indian example.
questions.solution_html:
• Chain ownership in media refers to a single company or group owning multiple outlets within
  • the same medium. For example, one corporation might own several different newspapers, a series of
  • radio stations, or a string of television channels across different cities or regions. This pattern allows
  • for centralized control over content, administration, and finance, leading to economies of scale but
  • potentially reducing the diversity of voices. One prominent Indian example of media chain ownership
  • is The Times of India Group (Bennett, Coleman & Co. Ltd.), which owns numerous newspapers like
  • The Times of India, The Economic Times, and Mumbai Mirror across India.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain how ownership pattern affects the edirorial policy of a media firm.
questions.solution_html:
• The ownership pattern of a media firm significantly impacts its editorial policy by
  • determining the ultimate goals, constraints, and ideological lens through which news is selected,
  • framed, and presented. This influence primarily operates through two mechanisms: commercial
  • interests and political or ideological agendas.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: What is native advertising? Give examples.
questions.solution_html:
• Native advertising is a form of paid media designed to seamlessly blend into the content,
  • look, and feel of the platform on which it appears, making it less intrusive than traditional banner or
  • pop-up ads. The goal is to provide valuable, engaging content that matches the user's browsing
  • experience, even though it is fundamentally commercial material, and it is usually required to be
  • clearly labeled as "sponsored" or "promoted."
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the significance of influencer marketing in social media.
questions.solution_html:
• Influencer marketing is highly significant in social media because it leverages the trust and
  • authenticity that content creators (influencers) have built with their dedicated audiences, enabling
  • brands to bypass traditional advertising skepticism and achieve higher levels of engagement and
  • conversion. Buiding trust, highly targeted reach, driving engagement and conversions,
  • competitiveness etc. are some factors.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the role of editors in content management.
questions.solution_html:
• The role of editors in content management is to act as the quality assurance gatekeepers and
  • strategic alignment coordinators for all published material, ensuring it is accurate, engaging, and
  • consistent with the organization's goals. Their role involves quality control & copyediting, factual
  • verification and accuracy check, style consistency and enforcement, content strategy alignment etc.
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Explain the major functions of management and discuss their relevance in the functioning of a
questions.solution_html:
• media house.
  • Planning: This involves setting the media house's goals and determining the best course of action to
  • achieve them. In a media house, planning means defining editorial direction, deciding on new
  • show/content launches, and creating media campaigns and budgets to maximize audience reach and
  • engagement.
  • Organizing: This is the function of structuring the workforce and resources. A media house must
  • establish clear departments (e.g., editorial, production, sales) and reporting lines to ensure efficient
  • content creation and timely delivery, especially crucial for fast-paced news cycles.
  • Staffing: This focuses on hiring, training, compensating, and evaluating the right personnel. For a
  • media house, staffing is critical for securing specialized talent, such as skilled journalists, creative
  • producers, and technical crews, to ensure the quality and credibility of content.
  • Directing (Leading): This is about guiding, motivating, and supervising employees. In a creative and
  • deadline-driven environment like a media house, directing involves providing leadership, fostering a
  • positive work culture, resolving conflicts, and communicating clear instructions to meet tight
  • broadcast or publication deadlines.
  • Controlling: This function involves setting performance standards, measuring actual results against
  • those standards, and taking corrective action. A media house uses controlling to monitor audience
  • ratings, analyze website traffic, track advertising revenue, and implement changes to ensure content
  • and financial objectives are consistently met.
